function: LSTM receiver for joint channel estimation and multi-user symbol detection in uplink IRS-assisted OFDM-NOMA, replacing SIC; IRS phases come from classical EBCD, not learned (pp. 3-5).
system: SISO uplink OFDM-NOMA, 2 users, 64 subcarriers, QPSK; passive reflecting IRS with 32 or 64 elements; carrier frequency band not stated (pp. 3, 6, Table 1).
method: Four-layer LSTM (input 384, output 128) plus fully connected 16-class output; supervised offline training with Adam, 50 epochs, then online testing (pp. 5, 6).
data_channel: Custom MATLAB simulation: Rician BS-IRS link (kappa 5 dB) and Rayleigh IRS-user links with distance path loss; 400,000 training and 160,000 test samples (pp. 5, 6).
test_conditions: Trained offline on simulated data, tested on 160,000 other samples; sweeps SNR, IRS elements (32/64), CP length (24/32), Rician versus Rayleigh; per-sweep training not stated (pp. 5-8).
baselines: Classical only: maximum-likelihood detector with perfect CSI, SIC with LS or MMSE channel estimation, and a no-IRS case; no learned baseline (pp. 3, 7).
metrics: Symbol error rate versus SNR for near and far users, plus training and validation accuracy (about 97%) and loss (about 0.1) curves (pp. 6, 7).
complexity: none: only qualitative 'low complexity' claims; no operations, parameter count, or runtime reported; training CPU named (pp. 3, 6).
openness: none: no code or data link and no public dataset; data generated in-house in MATLAB (p. 6).
q1_support: p. 5: "Rician channel model is employed for two-fold channel" and Rayleigh for the IRS-user links, both with distance path loss. This is a custom simulator; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 5: "offline using simulated data and then tested online"; the test set is 160,000 samples of the same simulator (page 6). The IRS-element, CP-length and Rician/Rayleigh sweeps never say a model trained in one condition was tested in another.
q3_support: p. 3: "The simulation results are benchmarked with maximum-likelihood detector (MLD)" and SIC with LS and MMSE, all non-learned. No earlier learned detector or standard network (FC, CNN) is compared; Figs. 5-8 show only LSTM, SIC and MLD.
q4_support: p. 3: "We propose a low complexity ML-based approach" is only a qualitative claim. No FLOPs, parameter count, order of complexity or runtime is reported; page 6 only says training "executed on a Core i7-7500U CPU".
q5_support: p. 6: "We created 400, 000 samples for training" with a MATLAB simulator; the paper gives no link to code or data and uses no public dataset of channels or signals.
notes: Included, area 1: the LSTM detects the symbols jointly with channel estimation and the main metric is SER. The IRS phase shifts come from the classical EBCD algorithm, so only the receiver is learned. The link is SISO but has an IRS, so the system check does not exclude it. q2 is 0 because the IRS-element, CP-length and fading sweeps may be separately trained models and the paper does not say; the reviewer may confirm on pages 7-8.
